result.abstractText:
Background

Rheumatoid arthritis remains a leading cause of irreversible joint disability worldwide. Triptolide and celastrol, major bioactive compounds derived from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F. (TwHF), have substantial therapeutic potential for rheumatoid arthritis. However, poor solubility, low oral bioavailability, narrow therapeutic windows, and dose-limiting systemic toxicity limit their clinical translation.

Objective

This review integrates the anti-rheumatoid arthritis mechanisms of triptolide and celastrol with recent advances in nanodelivery systems to establish a mechanism-guided framework for nanocarrier design and clinical translation.

Results

Triptolide and celastrol exert multifaceted anti-rheumatoid arthritis effects by inhibiting inflammatory signaling pathways, regulating macrophage polarization and T-cell homeostasis, suppressing fibroblast-like synoviocyte proliferation, and protecting bone and cartilage. Diverse nanodelivery platforms-including lipid-based, polymeric, inorganic, biomimetic, carrier-free, and hybrid systems-have substantially improved the bioavailability and lesion-targeting capability of triptolide and celastrol, achieving superior anti-inflammatory and joint-protective efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity.

Conclusion

Mechanism-guided nanodelivery may help translate triptolide and celastrol into safer, targeted rheumatoid arthritis therapies. Realizing this potential requires a shift from material-centric research toward application-oriented development supported by rigorous validation.

result.abstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by dysregulated immune responses and excessive keratinocyte proliferation, with substantial effects on patients' quality of life. Evidence suggests that the gut microbiota and the gut-skin-immune axis may contribute to systemic inflammation and immune dysregulation associated with psoriasis. This narrative review examines the potential immunomodulatory role of probiotics in psoriasis, with particular emphasis on strain-specific biological effects and the mechanisms linking intestinal microbial modulation to psoriasis-related inflammation. Probiotics may influence intestinal microbial composition, epithelial barrier integrity, microbial metabolite production, and immune signaling. Clinical studies have reported potential improvements in psoriasis severity, inflammatory biomarkers, or quality of life following probiotic supplementation; however, the available evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, with substantial variation in probiotic strains, formulations, doses, treatment durations, concomitant therapies, and clinical outcomes. Unlike previous systematic reviews and meta-analyses that primarily summarize clinical outcomes, this review integrates clinical findings with strain-specific mechanistic and experimental evidence to provide a biologically contextualized interpretation of the potential role of probiotics in psoriasis.

We included patients with PsA from an observational cohort and classified them into 3 groups: classical PsA (psoriasis diagnosed before PsA), concurrent disease (psoriasis and PsA diagnosed within 1 year), and antecedent PsA (PsA diagnosed > 1 year before psoriasis). We assessed the association between these groups and 2 outcomes: mean disease activity and the course of radiographic damage. We used multivariable linear regression to estimate the adjusted 5-year mean swollen joint count (SJC) and Cox proportional hazards regression to evaluate time to radiographic progression. Cox regression was also used to identify factors associated with psoriasis onset in the antecedent PsA group.

Results

Of the 1702 patients studied, 1138 (66.86%) were classified as having classical PsA, 444 (26.09%) as having concurrent PsA, and 120 (7.05%) as having antecedent PsA. These groups differed in baseline demographic and PsA-related characteristics. Compared with patients with classical PsA, those with concurrent or antecedent PsA showed no significant differences in time-averaged disease activity or time to radiographic progression. Biologic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (bDMARD) use was associated with a reduced risk of developing psoriasis in the group with antecedent PsA.

Conclusion

The relative order of psoriasis and PsA diagnosis does not significantly affect disease activity or radiographic progression. bDMARDs may influence the onset of psoriasis in patients with antecedent PsA.

Purpose

Psoriasis is a common chronic inflammatory skin disease with a high prevalence, which seriously impairs patients' quality of life. Although the clinical application of biologics has achieved satisfactory therapeutic effects, it still has certain limitations, such as high recurrence rate and poor clinical response in some patients. Therefore, it is urgent to further explore the pathogenesis of psoriasis to identify novel research directions and therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of this disease.

Methods

Conclusion

ASS1 serves as a critical regulator and promising therapeutic target for psoriasis. L-citrulline supplementation or ASS1 inhibition effectively blocks keratinocyte hyperactivation and retards psoriasis progression, providing a novel and feasible therapeutic strategy for psoriasis treatment.

Background

Although biologics are effective in treating psoriasis, a subset of patients experience severe relapse after treatment discontinuation.

Objective

To delineate the features and risk factors for a distinct pustular psoriasis flare following biologic withdrawal.

Methods

This multicenter study included treatment episodes from patients with psoriasis who responded to and subsequently discontinued biologic therapy between 2011 and 2025. Clinical features of this distinct pustular psoriasis flare were characterized, and associated factors were assessed using a generalized estimating equation model.

Results

These pustular psoriasis flares occurred in 86 of 1198 treatment episodes (7.2%) and were characterized by painful, diffuse, intense erythema with pustules and swelling, predominantly involving the lower limbs. The occurrence of these flares increased with a higher number of cycles of biologic withdrawal-relapse episodes. A family history of psoriasis, concomitant psoriatic arthritis, a prior episode of this flare phenotype, a higher number of previous biologic withdrawal-relapse episodes, and longer time to achieve Psoriasis Area and Severity Index 50 during biologic therapy were independently associated with this distinct pustular psoriasis flare.

Limitations

Nonrandomized allocation of treatment and lack of histologic and molecular data.

Conclusions

Vigilant monitoring and early treatment resumption are recommended for patients with risk factors for pustular psoriasis flares after biologic withdrawal.

result.abstractText: Choosing systemic therapy for psoriasis remains challenging in populations underrepresented in clinical trials, including pregnant and pediatric patients, patients with chronic infections, and those with difficult-to-treat phenotypes. Since the 2019 version of this article, therapeutic options have expanded substantially, including new pediatric approvals, oral targeted agents, and biologics with increasingly phenotype-specific evidence. Purpose

Psoriasis is a cutaneous and systemic inflammatory disease. Identifying biomarkers that accurately reflect disease activity and inflammatory burden has become an important area of research in psoriasis. Fecal calprotectin (FC), a noninvasive biomarker of neutrophil-driven inflammation, may provide complementary information in psoriasis. We aimed to assess FC levels in patients with psoriasis and to explore their association with disease characteristics.

Materials and methods

Eighty adult psoriasis patients and 80 healthy volunteers were included in this case-control study. None of the participants had active infection, pregnancy, malignancy, or known gastrointestinal disease. Demographic data, gastrointestinal complaints using the Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale, psoriasis severity using the Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) and Body Surface Area (BSA), and psoriasis characteristics were recorded. FC levels were measured by ELISA. ROC curve analysis and multivariable linear regression were performed.

Results

Median FC levels were significantly higher in psoriasis patients compared to controls (235.0 [11.2-2100.0] µg/g vs. 44.6 [6.7-711.6] µg/g, p < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated good discrimination between psoriasis patients and controls (AUC = 0.865), with an optimal cutoff value of 102 µg/g (sensitivity 87.5%, specificity 73.7%). FC levels showed a weak but significant positive correlation with psoriasis severity. Patients with FC levels >250 µg/g had significantly higher PASI and BSA scores than those with lower FC levels. In multivariable analysis, PASI remained independently associated with FC levels.

Conclusion

Psoriasis patients demonstrated elevated FC levels. FC levels were associated with psoriasis severity, suggesting that higher FC levels may parallel greater cutaneous disease burden. Baseline FC assessment requires further validation before clinical implementation.

result.abstractText: Objective Maternal diabetes during pregnancy is associated with long-term metabolic and immune-related outcomes in offspring. While psoriasis is strongly linked to metabolic comorbidities later in life, the impact of in utero exposure to maternal diabetes on psoriasis risk in offspring remains unknown. We investigated whether maternal diabetes during pregnancy is associated with the development of childhood psoriasis in offspring. Research Design and Methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study using electronic health record data from Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest health maintenance organization. The cohort included 215,280 singleton live births between 2010 and 2023, with follow-up through 2024. Maternal diabetes during pregnancy was identified using ICD-10 codes and categorized as gestational diabetes, type 1 diabetes, or type 2 diabetes. The primary outcome was childhood psoriasis in offspring. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis adjusted for maternal, pregnancy, and offspring characteristics were used to estimate associations. Results Overall, 5.4% of offspring were born to mothers with diabetes during pregnancy. During follow-up, 1,557 children (0.7%) were diagnosed with psoriasis. Psoriasis prevalence did not differ between offspring exposed and unexposed to maternal diabetes (0.7% vs. 0.7%). No associations were observed by diabetes subtype, treatment modality, or degree of glycemic control. In adjusted analyses, maternal diabetes was not associated with childhood psoriasis in offspring (HR 1.17, 95% CI 0.90-1.54; p = 0.246). Conclusions Maternal diabetes during pregnancy was not associated with increased childhood psoriasis risk in offspring. Our findings do not support a substantial role for prenatal metabolic dysregulation in childhood psoriasis development.

Background

Healthcare utilization in patients with psoriasis has been described from the perspective of psoriasis healthcare centers. Psoriasis healthcare utilization at the population level, including appointments with family physicians, impacts the overall financial expenditure.

Objectives

To describe the utilization of healthcare services in patients with psoriasis compared to the general non-psoriasis population.

Methods

We conducted a cross-sectional, population-based analysis of data from Clalit Health Services, the largest public health service provider in Israel, comparing the annual healthcare utilization and medication consumption of all Clalit members with psoriasis in 2023 with an age- and sex-matched group at a primary care clinic. We compared up to five non-psoriasis items.

Results

The study included 835,422 people (140,927 individuals with psoriasis and 694,671 without). Patients with psoriasis had more annual physician appointments than controls, and the meetings were longer. Patients with psoriasis took more sick leave and required more hospital admission compared to the control group. Tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors were prescribed much more often to patients with psoriasis than to the control group (3147 patients vs. 1857 in the matched control). More IL-17 blockers and IL-23 blockers were also prescribed more in the psoriasis group, although at a much lower level than the TNF inhibitors.

Conclusions

Patients with psoriasis used more healthcare services than the control group. Healthcare providers should allocate more resources to psoriasis care, both for primary care and at specialized psoriasis centers.

Background

The histopathological presentation of psoriasis may vary depending on the timing of the biopsy, prior treatments utilized, and the presence of secondary skin changes. Consequently, dermatopathologists play a pivotal role in ensuring an accurate diagnosis, particularly when the psoriatic histopathology deviates from the classic features. This study aims to compare the prevalence of classic and non-classic histopathologic features of psoriasis between untreated and treated psoriasis.

Methods

This is a review of 109 biopsies of psoriasis from 2015 to 2021 obtained from a single institution. The cases were reviewed by two independent dermatopathologists who were blinded to the assigned groups (untreated, n = 62, and treated, n = 47). A 20-item histopathologic grading criterion, comprising both classic and non-classic features of psoriasis, was used for assessment.

Results

The prevalence of both classic (p = 0.274; CI: -0.169, 0.593) and non-classic (p = 0.456; CI: -0.526, 0.236) histopathologic features of psoriasis did not differ between untreated (classic = 78%, non-classic = 27%) and treated (classic = 76%, non-classic = 29%) groups. A comparison of each histopathologic feature did not vary between groups (p > 0.05).

Conclusions

Psoriasis is a dynamic condition under the microscope. Classic histopathologic features of psoriasis seem to persist despite treatment. Non-classic features may also occur regardless of the treatment status. Hence, the presence of these features should not preclude the tissue diagnosis of psoriasis.

result.abstractText: Dysbiosis of the gut microbiota has been demonstrated to trigger immune responses that may heighten psoriasis susceptibility. However, conventional therapies for psoriasis are often limited by significant side effects. Ginsenoside Rk3 (Rk3), a bioactive triterpenoid glycoside compound derived from natural ginseng, has shown promise as a potent immunomodulator and gut regulator. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the potential protective effect of Rk3 against psoriasis, with a focus on the gut microbiota modulation and immune response regulation. Network pharmacology was first employed to predict potential targets for the action of Rk3 on psoriasis and an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis mice model was used to investigate the palliative effect of Rk3 on psoriasis. Our results reveal that Rk3 restores gut microbiota homeostasis, especially modulating the abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila and Parabacteroides distasonis, and effectively alleviates IMQ-induced psoriasis through gut microbiota-dependent mechanisms. Furthermore, Rk3 exerts a regulatory effect on aberrant amino acid metabolism, suppressing glutamine catabolism while enhancing short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) biosynthesis. Rk3-mediated regulation of glutamine metabolism exerts an inhibition effect on the conversion of glutamine to glutamate, suppresses Th17 cell differentiation and alleviates psoriasis via the IL-6/JAK1-STAT3 signaling axis. Overall, our research elucidates Rk3's mechanism of action in ameliorating psoriasis and highlights its potential as a gut microbiota modulator for psoriasis treatment.

result.abstractText: Psoriasis is associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity, but the extent and structure of the shared genetic architecture remain incompletely understood. We integrated large-scale European-ancestry genome-wide summary statistics for psoriasis and seven cardiovascular diseases to quantify genetic overlap, model shared liability and prioritize candidate mechanisms. Psoriasis showed modest genetic correlations with all cardiovascular outcomes, but mixture modelling estimated that more than half of psoriasis-associated non-zero variants were shared with five cardiovascular diseases. Genomic structural equation modelling of a latent psoriasis-CVD factor identified 167 independent risk loci, including 50 not genome-wide significant in any component trait. Multimodal prioritization nominated 473 candidate genes and 90 approved compounds with therapeutic relevance, including shared targets involving PDE4B, GLP1R, KEAP1 and PRDM16. Mediation and Mendelian randomization analyses implicated cardiometabolic traits, although no single trait accounted for more than half of the shared liability. These results prioritize genetic mechanisms and pharmacological hypotheses for psoriasis-associated cardiovascular multimorbidity.

Background

Psoriasis is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease that imposes a considerable burden of metabolic comorbidities. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is particularly common among patients with psoriasis, which may be attributed to shared metabolic and immune-inflammatory pathogenic pathways. However, evidence linking peripheral T-cell profiles to clinical phenotypes remains limited.

Methods

This is a cross-sectional study. A total of 408 participants were enrolled stratified into three groups: 206 patients with plaque psoriasis, 100 subjects undergoing routine health examinations (RHE group), and 102 patients with isolated MASLD. All participants underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) via FibroScan®, with simultaneous acquisition of Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) and Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAP). Comprehensive clinical and laboratory data were collected for further analysis. In a subset of 49 psoriasis participants (32 patients with psoriasis and MASLD and 17 patients with psoriasis alone), peripheral T-cell subpopulations were quantified using flow cytometry.

Results

Psoriasis patients had a higher MASLD prevalence than participants in RHE group (65.5% vs. 46.0%, P = 0.002), with psoriasis independently associated with MASLD (adjusted OR = 2.282, 95% CI: 1.181-4.408). Body mass index (BMI), hyperuricemia, insulin resistance-related indices (triglyceride glucose index [TyG], TyG-BMI), and uric acid-to-high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio (UHR) were linked to concomitant MASLD in psoriasis patients. Elevated liver enzymes were associated with severe hepatic steatosis grades. An exploratory model combining BMI, TyG and hyperuricemia exhibited favorable performance for MASLD screening, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.84 (95% CI, 0.78-0.89). Compared with patients with psoriasis alone, those with coexisting MASLD showed elevated circulating IL-17+ Th17 cells and an increased Th17/Treg ratio, and this immune imbalance correlated positively with the grade of hepatic steatosis.

Conclusion

Psoriasis is independently associated with MASLD. Psoriasis patients with coexisting MASLD present metabolic abnormalities along with peripheral Th17/Treg immune imbalance. The exploratory model combining BMI, the TyG index and hyperuricemia shows good performance for MASLD screening. These findings highlight the importance of multidisciplinary management for patients with psoriasis.

Psoriasis vulgaris is a chronic immune-mediated skin disorder characterized by keratinocyte hyperproliferation and T-cell-driven inflammation. Recent evidence suggests a potential role of gasdermin family proteins, particularly Gasdermin B (GSDMB), and the proinflammatory cytokine Interleukin-17A (IL-17A) in its pathogenesis.

Aims and objectives

To assess the gene expression levels of GSDMB and Interleukin-17A in patients with psoriasis vulgaris and explore their relationship with disease severity.

Patients and methods

This case-control study included 150 subjects: 75 patients with plaque psoriasis and 75 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Disease severity was assessed using the psoriasis area and severity index (PASI). Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction was performed on peripheral blood samples to measure GSDMB and IL-17A mRNA expression.

Results

The expression levels of both GSDMB and IL-17A were significantly elevated in psoriasis patients compared with controls ( P = 0.005 and P = 0.001, respectively). A strong positive association was also noted between GSDMB and IL-17A expression (r = 0.327, P = 0.004).

Limitations

result.abstractText: Research highlights the impact of experiencing a chronic skin condition upon psychosocial functioning. One such condition is psoriasis, an autoimmune inflammatory condition, resulting in red, scaly plaques occurring on the skin. People with psoriasis may experience body-image concerns related to the visibility of psoriasis, which negatively impacts relationships, engagement in valued activity, and wellbeing. This review aimed to synthesise qualitative research regarding appearance concerns of people with psoriasis, with a focus on the impact of altered appearance on psychosocial functioning. A systematic search of four databases (Academic Search Ultimate, Cinahl, Medline and Psychinfo) identified 26 papers for inclusion. Analysis was conducted utilising thematic synthesis to generate an integrated account regarding the experiences of psoriasis patients. Three themes were developed from the data: Constructing and navigating the psoriasis-identity; Appearance stigmatisation; and Acceptance and coping with an altered appearance. Although individual differences in adjustment and coping long-term were identified, findings highlight the impact of psoriasis upon identity and psychosocial functioning. Psychologists working within dermatology may drive systemic change by developing psycho-dermatological care frameworks and offering consultation and training within multidisciplinary teams. Targeted therapies may support psoriasis patients to develop acceptance, and positive body-image, thereby increasing wellbeing.

result.abstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder characterized by dysregulated epithelial-immune interactions. Emerging evidence implicates keratinocyte ferroptosis as a critical pathological mechanism, whereby oxidative epidermal damage and elevated levels of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) amplify immune dysregulation and sustain chronic psoriatic inflammation. Here, we developed a dual-action microneedle system (CAD), with needle tips composed of guanidine-functionalized chitosan and deferoxamine (DFO), designed to eliminate pro-inflammatory cfDNA while locally releasing DFO for iron chelation. In an imiquimod-induced psoriasis mouse model, CAD markedly alleviated psoriatic symptoms, reducing the psoriasis area and severity index score by approximately 50% compared with the model group and demonstrating superior therapeutic efficacy to clinically used calcipotriol. Further studies revealed that CAD depleted accumulated iron and inflammatory cfDNA in lesioned skin, alleviating oxidative stress and suppressing ferroptosis, inhibiting the inflammatory cascade, and maintaining immune homeostasis for effective psoriasis treatment. This study presents a dual-action microneedle therapy for psoriasis that alleviates psoriasis by modulating keratinocyte ferroptosis and scavenging cfDNA to restore inflammatory homeostasis, providing a promising foundation for the development of mechanism-guided combination therapies for psoriasis. Future work will further optimize the formulation for clinical translation and explore its therapeutic potential for other ferroptosis-related inflammatory skin disorders.

Patients with PsA have generally been analyzed as a single group regardless of psoriasis history, despite a reported association between psoriasis and TMJ involvement. To assess TMD symptoms, patient-reported outcome measures, and self-reported beneficial effects of systemic therapies and TMD-related treatment modalities in women with psoriatic arthritis, stratified by psoriasis history. The study included 27 women with self-reported PsA diagnosed within the healthcare system. Descriptive analyses were performed to describe socio-demographic, disease-related, TMD-related, and patient-reported outcome measures stratified by psoriasis history. Pain during jaw activity (77.8%), TMJ sounds (74.1%), and morning jaw stiffness/pain/fatigue (66.6%) were the most reported symptoms in the total sample. The proportions were higher among women with a history of psoriasis compared with those without a history of psoriasis (81.8% vs. 75.0%, 81.8% vs. 68.8%, and 72.7% vs. 62.5%, respectively). Occlusal adjustment in the psoriasis-history group and bite splint therapy in the other group were reported as the most received and most beneficial treatments in the respective. Women with PsA reported TMD symptoms and impaired patient-reported outcomes, with higher proportions reported in the psoriasis-history group. result.abstractText:
Background

International guidelines recommend screening individuals with psoriasis, a common chronic inflammatory skin condition, for a range of conditions across the spectrum of human disease. Despite this, gaps may remain within our knowledge of the full breadth of comorbidity in psoriasis.

Objectives

To perform a phenome-wide longitudinal association study of psoriasis and its comorbidities.

Method

We conducted cohort studies (matched for age, sex and general practice) for each block (group of related conditions) of outcomes within the International Classification of Diseases - Clinical Modification (10th ed.) using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum primary care data linked to secondary care Hospital Episode Statistics (to define ICD outcomes) within the United Kingdom. We evaluated the association between psoriasis and outcomes in the first year of diagnosis and in the subsequent period. We estimated hazard ratios (HR) with 99% confidence intervals from Cox regression, with covariate models adjusted for alcohol, smoking, BMI and measures of social deprivation.

Results

We compared 320,220 individuals with psoriasis to 1,706,424 matched individuals. In 225 ICD blocks evaluated, psoriasis was associated with numerous outcomes across organ systems. Strong, non-dermatological associations in the long-term included liver disease (HR 1.47 [1.42-1.51], RD 1.16), substance (including alcohol and tobacco) misuse (HR 1.26 [1.25-1.28], RD 3.27) and other respiratory diseases principally affecting the interstitium (HR 1.33 [1.27-1.40], RD 0.31).

Conclusion

This study provides evidence of association between psoriasis and a range of comorbidity and may serve to generate hypotheses on previously underappreciated associations.

result.abstractText: Psoriasis is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory disease with impacts beyond the skin and joints. Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and excessive alcohol consumption are common in the psoriasis population, affecting up to two-thirds of patients. Interleukin-17 (IL-17) has been identified as a potential key pro-inflammatory link between psoriasis and MASLD. IL-17 levels have been positively correlated with progression of MASLD to more advanced forms of liver disease, including steatohepatitis, cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma. Given the high prevalence of concurrent psoriasis and liver disease, dermatologists should have an elevated index of suspicion of MASLD in patients with psoriasis, particularly those with concomitant metabolic risk factors and/or excessive alcohol consumption. Using 3 parameters, the Fibrosis-4 index is a validated, non-invasive screening tool that can be implemented in clinical practice. With the wide variety of therapeutics available to treat psoriasis, practitioners should be mindful of systemic agents carrying potential hepatotoxic adverse effects and could consider instead implementation of advanced therapies that have neutral or potentially beneficial effects on the liver. There is emerging data, pending larger prospective confirmatory studies, that support consideration of IL-17 inhibitors as a reasonable option in appropriate patients with or at risk of MASLD.

Background

Psoriasis is increasingly recognized as a systemic inflammatory disease and has been associated with chronic kidney disease. Whether psoriasis is also linked to subclinical impairment in renal microcirculation remains unclear.

Objective

To assess renal functional reserve (RFR) in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis using the renal stress test (RST).

Methods

Fifty-one consecutive adults with psoriasis and 35 age- and sex-matched controls underwent RST. Renal resistive index (RRI) was measured by Doppler ultrasound in an interlobular renal artery at baseline and after abdominal compression with a fluid-filled bag corresponding to 10% of body weight. Intrarenal resistive index variation (IRRIV) was calculated as the percentage difference between baseline and stress values.

Results

Patients with psoriasis showed a lower IRRIV than controls (median 13.8% [10.7-18.6] vs 23.1% [17.8-25.0]; p<0.001). IRRIV differed significantly across controls and Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) severity strata (p<0.001), but post hoc pairwise comparisons showed that this difference was driven by the comparison between controls and psoriasis patients, with no significant difference between severity strata. In multivariable analysis, psoriasis remained independently associated with lower IRRIV.

Limitations

This was a single-center pilot study with a limited sample size.

Conclusion

Moderate-to-severe psoriasis was associated with impaired renal functional reserve, suggesting subclinical renal microcirculatory dysfunction. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and define their clinical relevance.

Hence, the study investigated the therapeutic effects of quercetin against psoriasis and elucidated its underlying molecular mechanisms, with a focus on AKR1B10-mediated glycolytic reprogramming. Flow cytometry as well as ELISA were performed to assess T helper 17 (Th17) cell proportions and systemic inflammatory responses. Candidate therapeutic targets of quercetin in psoriasis treatment were obtained by integrating GEO database analysis, target prediction, and machine learning algorithms. A series of assays were harnessed to measure AKR1B10 expression and glycolysis-related enzymes, lactic acid, and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR). Overexpressing AKR1B10 largely negated suppressive impacts of quercetin on keratinocyte glycolysis and proliferation. Quercetin alleviates inflammation and abnormal keratinocyte proliferation in experimental psoriasis-like models, potentially through modulation of AKR1B10-associated glycolytic reprogramming.

result.abstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disorder marked by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and persistent immune activation. Identifying genetically supported druggable genes may offer new avenues for therapeutic development. We performed Mendelian randomization and colocalization analyses to identify druggable genes associated with psoriasis. Drug screening and molecular docking further indicated that SLC15A2 could be modulated by small molecules. Overall, these results suggest that SLC15A2 is a potential pathogenic gene with therapeutic relevance in psoriasis, providing insights into its role in keratinocyte hyperproliferation.

result.abstractText:
Background & aims

Evidence suggests that patients with inflammatory bowel disease are at higher risk of psychiatric disorders, yet temporal pattern of risk elevation before/after inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis and role of familial factors remain unclear.

Methods

Swedish patients with inflammatory bowel disease diagnosed between 2007 and 2023 were compared with reference individuals in a matched population-based cohort and compared with inflammatory bowel disease-free full siblings in a sibling-controlled cohort. Primary outcome was any psychiatric disorder, whereas secondary outcomes included psychotic disorders, mood disorders, anxiety disorders, eating disorders, substance misuse, personality disorders, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and autism spectrum disorders. We estimated temporal patterns of hazard ratios from 5 years before to 10 years after inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis by using flexible parametric survival models.

Results

The study included 43,862 patients with inflammatory bowel disease (mean age at diagnosis, 41.6 years; 47.3% female) and 178,821 reference individuals. The hazard ratio of any psychiatric disorder started to increase from 2 to 3 years before inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis (eg, hazard ratio, 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 1.09-1.21 at -2 years), peaked immediately after inflammatory bowel disease diagnosis (hazard ratio, 1.50; 95% confidence interval, 1.41-1.59 at 0.5 year), and decreased rapidly thereafter but remained increased even at 10 years after diagnosis (hazard ratio, 1.19; 95% confidence interval, 1.13-1.24). The increased hazard ratio was mainly driven by major depressive disorder, anxiety disorders, and substance misuse. No increase was observed for psychotic disorders, personality disorders, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, although patients with inflammatory bowel disease were more likely to have autism spectrum disorders shortly after diagnosis and eating disorders from ≥5 years onwards. Similar temporal hazard ratio patterns were observed across all subtypes of inflammatory bowel disease: Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, and inflammatory bowel disease-unclassified. Similar risk increases for psychiatric disorders were observed in the sibling-controlled cohort.

Conclusions

Patients with inflammatory bowel disease were at an increased risk of several psychiatric disorders from 2 to 3 years before diagnosis through up to 10 years after, and this risk increase cannot be fully explained by shared familial factors.
